text:
Stonebeck advances toward resolution despite redemption gate

Rating: overweight

The redemption gate at Stonebeck Credit reads, in our house view, as a liquidity mechanism rather than a solvency verdict. Gates exist precisely to prevent forced selling into air pockets — and the reported_vs_public_gap of +1.0% supports that reading: internal marks sit above where secondary desks are currently clearing paper in the low 80s. That gap is the market overshooting on panic pricing while the manager holds a firmer, arguably more accurate, view of underlying value. Grimshaw's language of "fragilities compounding beneath stable marks" inverts this: we read the same spread between reported and public prices as evidence the public tape is the noisy signal, not the reported book.

Contextualize the drawdown of -3.0% and ytd_return of -3.5% against the one_year_return of +6.0%. A vehicle that has still delivered a positive twelve-month print through a period where hy_spread_now_bps has widened to 640bps is demonstrating carry res
